about: The tools and the instructions of the Nuclear MCP server.

rows.title: `api_inspect` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Fetches a public API's url and answers the shape of its JSON (keys, types, nested objects, a paged answer).
body: Fetches a public API's url and answers the shape of its JSON (keys, types, nested objects, a paged answer). With project, component and name it also shows the files generate_resource would write from it.

rows.title: `app_add` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Add an app to a workspace: `nuclear new` makes it in a folder of the workspace and the marker names it.
body: Add an app to a workspace: `nuclear new` makes it in a folder of the workspace and the marker names it. app: its name (its folder); platform: mobile, web or backend; dialect: optional (the platform's default). Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

rows.title: `app_remove` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Remove an app from a workspace (the marker stops naming it); its folder is deleted only with delete_folder true (every file in it: only when the user asked for it).
body: Remove an app from a workspace (the marker stops naming it); its folder is deleted only with delete_folder true (every file in it: only when the user asked for it). Asks the user first, saying which (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

rows.title: `app_rename` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Rename an app of a workspace (new_name: its new name).
body: Rename an app of a workspace (new_name: its new name). Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

rows.title: `generate_component` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A new component of the project with its facade (appcomponent).
body: A new component of the project with its facade (appcomponent).

rows.title: `generate_resource` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The finished, compiling code of a resource: its models, the repository, one use case per action, the facade's aliases, the controller (backend) or, with screen, a screen with its state manager (mobile, web), and the tests.
body: The finished, compiling code of a resource: its models, the repository, one use case per action, the facade's aliases, the controller (backend) or, with screen, a screen with its state manager (mobile, web), and the tests. The fields: from_json (an example answer of the API: a url, which also gives the API, or a file), from_spec (a spec.md: its example answer or its Key | Type table, and its `GET <url>` line), or fields ("id:int name:string origin:Origin?"). source: "rest:<base url>", "rest" or "db" (backend only). actions: of list, get, search, create, update, delete (default: list and get for an API, the rest for a database). dry_run shows the files without writing them. Nothing is overwritten; a name declared elsewhere stops it.

rows.title: `generate_screen` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A screen of a mobile or web project with its state manager and state model, for a view that is not a list of a resource (generate_resource with screen writes those).
body: A screen of a mobile or web project with its state manager and state model, for a view that is not a list of a resource (generate_resource with screen writes those).

rows.title: `generate_usecase` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A use case wired into its component: its alias in the facade and, with route (backend), its route in the controller of the route's prefix ("POST orders/{id}/cancel": a {name} is a parameter of the use case; the controller is created when missing).
body: A use case wired into its component: its alias in the facade and, with route (backend), its route in the controller of the route's prefix ("POST orders/{id}/cancel": a {name} is a parameter of the use case; the controller is created when missing). With calls ("OrderRepository.pending": a method that repository declares) the use case is written too, because it only calls that method. Without calls the use case must already be in the project: one with rules of its own is written first, then this wires it. dry_run shows the files without writing them.

rows.title: `graph_answer` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The exact answer to a question that has one (every command of a tool, the tools of this server and their parameters, the commands that write a kind, a diagnostic by its code, the stages of the Builder, the members of a base type, a version...): the rows of the graph's database, whole, never recalled; then the cards the shelves answer by meaning.
body: The exact answer to a question that has one (every command of a tool, the tools of this server and their parameters, the commands that write a kind, a diagnostic by its code, the stages of the Builder, the members of a base type, a version...): the rows of the graph's database, whole, never recalled; then the cards the shelves answer by meaning. Prefer it to graph_search for "which", "list", "what are the" questions. platform: backend, mobile or web.

rows.title: `graph_card` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: One row of the graph by its id, with what it links to: error:N0114 (a diagnostic), kind:backend.usecase, decorator:backend.get, tool:nuclear.gen.resource, mcp:generate_resource, lib:string, platform:mobile, layout:web, playbook:<name>, concept:<name>.
body: One row of the graph by its id, with what it links to: error:N0114 (a diagnostic), kind:backend.usecase, decorator:backend.get, tool:nuclear.gen.resource, mcp:generate_resource, lib:string, platform:mobile, layout:web, playbook:<name>, concept:<name>.

rows.title: `graph_monitor` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: project_monitor, and the hot spots kept in the graph (`monitor:<project>`) so later sessions know where the app was slow.
body: project_monitor, and the hot spots kept in the graph (`monitor:<project>`) so later sessions know where the app was slow. Call it after a run with `nuclear run --monitor`.

rows.title: `graph_prompt` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The validated prompt of a use case: feature, refactor, bug, docs, diagram, test, security, piece, plan.
body: The validated prompt of a use case: feature, refactor, bug, docs, diagram, test, security, piece, plan.

rows.title: `graph_remember` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Keep a decision, a name or a solved example (collection examples: the task, then the validated .nuc) so later sessions find it.
body: Keep a decision, a name or a solved example (collection examples: the task, then the validated .nuc) so later sessions find it.

rows.title: `graph_search` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Search the Nuclear Smart Graph, by meaning and by exact name (a diagnostic code, a command, a kind).
body: Search the Nuclear Smart Graph, by meaning and by exact name (a diagnostic code, a command, a kind). shelf: concepts (what it is, why, how it works), language (how it is written in Nuclear), platforms (kinds, decorators, layout, plugins), tools (CLI commands, MCP tools, HTTP routes, generators, agents), errors (diagnostics, failures and their fixes), capabilities (what can and cannot be done, limits), playbooks (procedures, roles, skills), examples (validated Nuclear), docs (the long documents: dialects, ADRs, context, status), memory (what agents kept about projects); several separated by commas; "" searches every shelf. platform: backend, mobile, web. kind: a kind's rows (usecase, repository...). type: a row type (diagnostic, kind, cli, playbook...). Each card comes with the rows it links to.

rows.title: `graph_strategy` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Which kind of request this is (a whole system, a component, a resource, one screen, a use case, a rename, a failing test, a question...) and the plan of that kind, step by step with the tool of each step.
body: Which kind of request this is (a whole system, a component, a resource, one screen, a use case, a rename, a failing test, a question...) and the plan of that kind, step by step with the tool of each step. Call it first, with the user's request in their own words, and follow the plan it answers. platform: backend, mobile or web.

rows.title: `member_add` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Hire members into a team: role (analyst, architect, developer, qa, devops), and optionally employee (of the roster), kind (agent or api), provider, model (one this machine has), name, count.
body: Hire members into a team: role (analyst, architect, developer, qa, devops), and optionally employee (of the roster), kind (agent or api), provider, model (one this machine has), name, count. Never the local kind (the local models are on standby). Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

rows.title: `member_edit` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Change a member of a team (member: its id in the team): who works it (kind agent or api, provider, model), its employee, name, instructions, temperament or skills (the whole list).
body: Change a member of a team (member: its id in the team): who works it (kind agent or api, provider, model), its employee, name, instructions, temperament or skills (the whole list). Never the local kind (the local models are on standby). Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

rows.title: `member_remove` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Let a member go (member: its id in the team).
body: Let a member go (member: its id in the team). Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

rows.title: `nuclear_brief` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The short sheet of Nuclear and a platform (backend, mobile, web), or a dialect: read it before writing .nuc.
body: The short sheet of Nuclear and a platform (backend, mobile, web), or a dialect: read it before writing .nuc.

rows.title: `nuclear_build` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: What a piece of Nuclear becomes in the dialect's language (Python, TypeScript, Dart).
body: What a piece of Nuclear becomes in the dialect's language (Python, TypeScript, Dart).

rows.title: `nuclear_check` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Errors of a piece of Nuclear (code) or of a whole project (path of its folder): `ok` or one line per error with its fix.
body: Errors of a piece of Nuclear (code) or of a whole project (path of its folder): `ok` or one line per error with its fix.

rows.title: `nuclear_defs` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A declaration of the type definitions (a class or Class.member of a library the dialect uses).
body: A declaration of the type definitions (a class or Class.member of a library the dialect uses). With the project's folder, also of a package the project added (nuclear add <package>).

rows.title: `nuclear_doc` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: One topic of the atlas, whole (nuclear_start lists them): a guide chapter (syntax, functions, control...), base, library, a platform (mobile, backend, web), a dialect (flutter, fastapi, nestjs, react), a tool (cli, mcp, vscode, builder...), context-docs, example/<name>.
body: One topic of the atlas, whole (nuclear_start lists them): a guide chapter (syntax, functions, control...), base, library, a platform (mobile, backend, web), a dialect (flutter, fastapi, nestjs, react), a tool (cli, mcp, vscode, builder...), context-docs, example/<name>. A word that is not a topic answers the topics that explain it.

rows.title: `nuclear_env` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The environments of a Synapsis project (spec 021): every env("NAME", "default") of its code and the values of each environment (.env, .env.<environment>, their .local versions, the system's keyring).
body: The environments of a Synapsis project (spec 021): every env("NAME", "default") of its code and the values of each environment (.env, .env.<environment>, their .local versions, the system's keyring). action: list (JSON: every variable × every environment, required ones without a value are null; env alone: that one), envs (the environments and the active one), set (name, value; env: that environment, else the shared .env; local: the .local file of this machine), unset (name; secret: the keyring's), use (env: the project's active one). A secret is never set here: its value must not pass through a model; ask the user to run `nuclear env set NAME --secret --env <environment>` in a terminal, which reads it hidden.

rows.title: `nuclear_fmt` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: The piece of Nuclear in the canonical layout.
body: The piece of Nuclear in the canonical layout.

rows.title: `nuclear_help` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Documentation of a kind, decorator, header word (with dialect), a topic or a command.
body: Documentation of a kind, decorator, header word (with dialect), a topic or a command.

rows.title: `nuclear_project` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: A `nuclear` command in a project of the framework: new, build, install, test, check, analyze, make (g), migrate, add, remove, explain.
body: A `nuclear` command in a project of the framework: new, build, install, test, check, analyze, make (g), migrate, add, remove, explain. Example: command="make", args=["component", "orders"]. A library the project lacks (npm, PyPI, pub.dev): command="add", args=["lodash"] installs it and generates its type definitions.

rows.title: `nuclear_start` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: CALL FIRST, before anything about Nuclear: what NuclearLang and Synapsis are, the rules never broken, the work cycle with these tools on this machine, and the atlas of every topic (the language, the library, each platform and dialect, the tools, how a project documents itself, validated examples), each read with nuclear_doc.
body: CALL FIRST, before anything about Nuclear: what NuclearLang and Synapsis are, the rules never broken, the work cycle with these tools on this machine, and the atlas of every topic (the language, the library, each platform and dialect, the tools, how a project documents itself, validated examples), each read with nuclear_doc. With project (a folder inside a Synapsis project), also its platform, its pieces and the syntax sheet of its dialect.

rows.title: `project_inspect` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: What a Synapsis project has: its platform and dialect, its components with their declarations by kind, and the generators of its platform.
body: What a Synapsis project has: its platform and dialect, its components with their declarations by kind, and the generators of its platform. Call it before generating or writing, so nothing is declared twice.

rows.title: `project_monitor` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Where the app is slow (Nuclear Monitor): the hot spots (slow, async calls in a loop, many connections, much memory) and the time of each Nuclear function and method, from the last run with `nuclear run --monitor`.
body: Where the app is slow (Nuclear Monitor): the hot spots (slow, async calls in a loop, many connections, much memory) and the time of each Nuclear function and method, from the last run with `nuclear run --monitor`.

rows.title: `project_run_log` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Why the app failed or what it did: the tail of the project's run log `.nuclear/logs/run.log` (lines: default 200, at most 2000), which `nuclear run` and the editor's devices write: each step (build, install, serve, the device), the build's errors, the server's output, `failed:` and `exited:`.
body: Why the app failed or what it did: the tail of the project's run log `.nuclear/logs/run.log` (lines: default 200, at most 2000), which `nuclear run` and the editor's devices write: each step (build, install, serve, the device), the build's errors, the server's output, `failed:` and `exited:`. Read it after a run that failed.

rows.title: The Nuclear MCP server: its tools and how a client must work with them
rows.summary: `nuclear-mcp` speaks the Model Context Protocol over stdio and gives an AI client 47 tools: the Smart Graph, the compiler, the `nuclear` commands, the generators, the internet and the local developer.
body: NuclearLang (.nuc) and Synapsis, its framework. Nothing about Nuclear is in your training and it is not TypeScript, Dart nor Python: before anything about Nuclear (a .nuc file, the nuclear command, a Synapsis project, a question about them), call nuclear_start. It answers what Nuclear is, the rules never broken, the work cycle on this machine and the atlas of every topic, each read with nuclear_doc. Never search the disk for Nuclear's sources and never guess a syntax. A product is made with these tools: never write target code (TypeScript, Dart, Python) for a feature nor translate code into Nuclear by hand; when a tool cannot do something, say so. Work starts from a workspace (workspace_show of the user's folder; workspace_create and app_add for a new product), and every change of a workspace, an app, a spec or a team is asked to the user first. Then, for a request, call graph_strategy with the user's own words and follow its plan.

rows.title: `skills_set` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server

body: Set the library skills of a team (every member inherits them) or, with member, of one member: skills is the whole list of skill ids (Nuclear Builder's `skills list` names them). Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

rows.summary: Write a new spec of a project where Nuclear Builder reads it (it shows in the Builder at once): its title, its business component (a folder of components/, or _global for the whole project), its acceptance criteria (each one checkable: ask the user for them when they are not given), and optionally its layer (presentation, domain or data), its use case (feature, refactor, bug, test, security,…
body: Write a new spec of a project where Nuclear Builder reads it (it shows in the Builder at once): its title, its business component (a folder of components/, or _global for the whole project), its acceptance criteria (each one checkable: ask the user for them when they are not given), and optionally its layer (presentation, domain or data), its use case (feature, refactor, bug, test, security, docs, diagram) and its description; or text: the spec's whole markdown, from its `# title`. Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

body: Replace the text of a spec (its whole markdown, from its `# title`; spec_show gives the current one). Asks the user first (confirm: the token of a preview, when the client cannot ask).

rows.title: `workspace_create` — a tool of the Nuclear MCP server
rows.summary: Create a workspace: a folder that organizes one business project and the apps that form it, recognized by its marker `.workspace/workspace.nuc` (the editor, this server and the agents start from it).
body: Create a workspace: a folder that organizes one business project and the apps that form it, recognized by its marker `.workspace/workspace.nuc` (the editor, this server and the agents start from it). path: where (the folder is made); name (default: the folder's name) and description.
